title: Multi-step real-world problems
blurb: Plan, solve and check money, time, rate and dosage word problems that take two or more steps.
question: A nursing assistant earns $18.50 an hour and works 32 hours. From that pay she covers rent of $425, groceries of $96.40 and gas of $54.75. How much is left, and how do you avoid stopping one step short?

teach.body: Formally, a multi-step problem needs two or more operations, where the result of one step feeds the next. In plain English: the answer is at the end of a chain, and the TEAS puts the links of that chain (the intermediate values) among the wrong options. Work to a plan: know exactly what is being asked, in which units, before you touch the calculator.

steps.label: Read the last line
steps.sub: what is asked, in what units?

teach.h: Worked example: a 750 mL IV bag
items: Asked: how much is LEFT after a nurse uses 2/5 of a 750 mL bag, then 1/3 of the remainder?
Step 1: used first = 2/5 × 750 = 300 mL. Remainder = 750 − 300 = 450 mL.
Step 2: used next = 1/3 × 450 = 150 mL (1/3 of the remainder, not of 750).
Check: 300 + 150 + 300 = 750 mL. ✓ Note 450 (the remainder) is an intermediate value, not the answer.

teach.h: Worked example: elapsed time and the 24-hour clock
items: 2:45 p.m. to 5:10 p.m.: count whole hours, 2:45 → 4:45 = 2 h.
Then the minutes: 4:45 → 5:10 = 15 + 10 = 25 min. Total: 2 h 25 min.
Check in minutes past noon: 5:10 = 310 and 2:45 = 165; 310 − 165 = 145 min = 2 h 25 min. ✓
Never subtract times as decimals: 5.10 − 2.45 = 2.65 means nothing, because an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.

teach.caption: After noon, add 12 to the hour: 2:30 p.m. → 14:30 → 1430.

teach.h: Worked examples: unit price and rate
items: Better buy: 18 oz for $4.32 or 28 oz for $6.44? Unit prices: 4.32 ÷ 18 = $0.24/oz; 6.44 ÷ 28 = $0.23/oz. The 28 oz size is cheaper per ounce.
Rate: 150 miles in 2.5 hours. Speed = distance ÷ time = 150 ÷ 2.5 = 60 mph.
Units guide the operation: miles ÷ hours = miles per hour.

teach.caption: The bars add back to the paycheck: 425 + 96.40 + 54.75 + 15.85 = 592.

teach.text: The four multi-step traps: stopping at an intermediate value (the remainder, the subtotal); answering "how many more" with a total; mixing units (minutes with hours, mL with L, cents with dollars); and rounding a count the wrong way (round up for "how many boxes needed," down for "how many full doses").

teach.body: Tyrone Jackson, a nursing assistant saving for nursing school, earns $18.50 an hour for 32 hours: 18.50 × 32 = $592.00. Bills: 425 + 96.40 + 54.75 = $576.15. Left: 592.00 − 576.15 = $15.85. Estimate: 18 × 32 ≈ 580 and bills ≈ 425 + 100 + 55 = 580, so a small amount left is reasonable. ✓

items: Read the last line first: what is asked, and in what units?
Write each step's result with its unit; the last step answers the question.
Elapsed time: count hours, then minutes; never subtract times as decimals.
Check units, estimate, and watch for intermediate values among the options.

summary: You can now plan and solve multi-step money, time, rate, supply and dosage problems: read what is asked, chain the operations, keep units straight and check the result. You also spot the intermediate-value and unit-mixing options the TEAS plants.

A.q: During a shift a patient drank 240 mL of juice, 1 1/2 cups of water and 180 mL of broth. Use 1 cup = 240 mL. What was the patient's total intake in milliliters?

whyNot.1: 660 counts the water as 1 cup (240 mL) instead of 1 1/2 cups.
whyNot.3: 600 leaves out the 180 mL of broth.

A.q: A patient's IV infusion started at 10:50 a.m. and finished at 2:25 p.m. the same day. How long did it run?
A.why: Whole hours: 10:50 → 1:50 = 3 h. Minutes: 1:50 → 2:25 = 10 + 25 = 35 min. Total 3 h 35 min.

whyNot.1: 4 h 15 min subtracts the times like decimals (14.25 − 10.50 = 3.75, read as 3 h 75 min).
whyNot.2: 4 h 25 min subtracts the hours (14 − 10) and then the minutes backward (50 − 25).
whyNot.3: 2 h 35 min miscounts the hours: 10:50 to 1:50 is 3 hours.

A.q: A bottle holds 90 tablets. A patient takes 1 1/2 tablets three times a day. How many days will the bottle last?

whyNot.0: 30 divides by the 3 doses but ignores that each dose is 1 1/2 tablets.
whyNot.2: 60 divides by one dose (1.5) instead of the daily amount (4.5).

B.q: Isabella has $150. She buys 3 sets of scrubs at $24.95 each and a pair of shoes for $38.50. How much money does she have left?

whyNot.0: $86.55 subtracts the price of one set of scrubs instead of three.
whyNot.1: $113.35 is the amount spent, an intermediate value; the question asks what is left.

B.q: An ambulance travels 18 miles at an average speed of 45 miles per hour. How many minutes does the trip take?
B.why: Time = distance ÷ speed = 18 ÷ 45 = 0.4 hour. Convert: 0.4 × 60 = 24 minutes.

whyNot.1: 40 min reads 0.4 hour as 40 minutes; an hour has 60 minutes, so 0.4 h = 24 min.
whyNot.2: 2.5 divides speed by distance (45 ÷ 18); time is distance ÷ speed.
whyNot.3: 810 multiplies distance by speed; d = r × t means t = d ÷ r.

B.q: A nurse gave 3 doses of 125 mg in the morning and 2 doses of 250 mg in the evening. How many more milligrams were given in the evening than in the morning?
B.why: Morning: 3 × 125 = 375 mg. Evening: 2 × 250 = 500 mg. Difference: 500 − 375 = 125 mg.

whyNot.0: 875 mg is the total for the day; "how many more" asks for a difference.
whyNot.1: 500 mg is the evening total, an intermediate value.
whyNot.3: 375 mg is the morning total, an intermediate value.

C.q: A 1,200 mL bag of fluid is hung. One fourth of it is infused before lunch, and 2/3 of the remainder is infused after lunch. How much fluid is left in the bag?
C.why: Before lunch: 1/4 × 1,200 = 300 mL, leaving 900 mL. After lunch: 2/3 × 900 = 600 mL. Left: 900 − 600 = 300 mL. Check: 300 + 600 + 300 = 1,200.

whyNot.0: 900 mL is what remained after the first quarter was infused, an intermediate value; 2/3 of it still has to come out.
whyNot.2: 100 mL takes 2/3 of the whole bag (800 mL) instead of 2/3 of the remainder.
whyNot.3: 600 mL is the amount infused after lunch, not the amount left.

C.q: A 1,000 mL IV bag is started at 0830 at 125 mL per hour. At 1030 the rate is increased to 150 mL per hour. At what time, on the 24-hour clock, will the bag finish?

whyNot.0: 1630 ignores the rate change and runs the whole bag at 125 mL/h (8 h from 0830).
whyNot.1: 1710 runs all 1,000 mL at 150 mL/h from 1030 (6 h 40 min), forgetting the 250 mL already infused.
whyNot.2: 1330 adds the 5 hours to the start time (0830) instead of to 1030.

C.q: A patient uses 2 puffs of an inhaler twice a day. Each inhaler holds 200 puffs. How many full weeks will one inhaler last?
C.why: Per day: 2 × 2 = 4 puffs. Days: 200 ÷ 4 = 50. Weeks: 50 ÷ 7 = 7.14, and only full weeks count, so 7.

whyNot.0: 8 rounds 7.14 up, but the inhaler runs out partway through the 8th week.
whyNot.1: 50 is the number of days, an intermediate value; the question asks for weeks.
whyNot.3: 14 counts 2 puffs a day instead of 4 (200 ÷ 2 = 100 days ÷ 7).

reteach.title: A word problem is a road trip
reteach.question: You leave for a clinical placement 42 miles away at 6:50 a.m. and average 56 mph. When do you arrive, and why can't you jump straight to the destination?

blocks.h: Each leg ends where the next begins
blocks.body: A GPS doesn't teleport you: it plans legs. Leg 1 turns distance and speed into travel time: 42 ÷ 56 = 0.75 h = 45 min. Leg 2 adds that time to the start: 6:50 + 45 min = 7:35 a.m. The travel time (45 min) is a waypoint, not the destination. On the TEAS, waypoints appear as wrong options to catch anyone who stops early.

items: Reasonable? 56 mph is nearly a mile a minute, so 42 miles in about 45 minutes fits.

blocks.text: 0.75 hour is 45 minutes, not 75 minutes. Convert decimal hours by multiplying by 60.

explain.body: Underline what is asked. "How many more" and "how much is left" are differences, not totals. Every value you compute on the way is a possible wrong option.

test.q: A clinic has 480 flu shots. It gives 135 on Monday and 162 on Tuesday. How many more shots must it give to use all of them?
test.why: Given so far: 135 + 162 = 297. Still to give: 480 − 297 = 183. Check: 297 + 183 = 480.

whyNot.1: 297 is the number already given, an intermediate value.
whyNot.2: 27 is the difference between Monday and Tuesday, not what remains.
whyNot.3: 777 adds every number in the problem.

explain.body: Count whole hours to a matching time, then add the leftover minutes. On the 24-hour clock, a shift from 1845 to 0715 crosses midnight.

test.q: A night shift runs from 1845 to 0715 the next morning. How long is the shift?
test.why: 1845 to 0645 is 12 hours; 0645 to 0715 is 30 minutes. Total 12 h 30 min.

whyNot.0: 11 h 30 min subtracts the clock numbers as plain numbers (1845 − 0715 = 1130).
whyNot.2: 13 h 10 min treats clock times as decimals (3115 − 1845 = 1270, read as 12 h 70 min).
whyNot.3: 13 h 30 min counts the hours from 18 to 7 and adds the 30 minutes instead of subtracting them.

explain.body: A rate is one quantity per one unit of another. Let the units decide: miles ÷ hours gives miles per hour. 15 minutes is 1/4 hour, so scale up by 4.

test.q: A patient in cardiac rehab walks 0.6 mile in 15 minutes. At this rate, what is the patient's speed in miles per hour?
test.why: 15 minutes = 1/4 hour, so in 1 hour: 0.6 × 4 = 2.4 miles. Speed = 2.4 mph.

whyNot.0: 0.04 is miles per MINUTE (0.6 ÷ 15), an intermediate value.
whyNot.1: 9 multiplies 0.6 × 15 instead of converting to hours.
whyNot.2: 25 divides 15 by 0.6, which gives minutes per mile, not miles per hour.

explain.body: Find the total coming in, find the total going out, then subtract. Line up decimal points and keep cents.

test.q: Jamal earns $16.25 an hour and works 24 hours. He pays $45.50 for a textbook and $112 for a uniform. How much of his pay is left?

whyNot.0: $390.00 is his pay before costs, an intermediate value.
